newsitem.title: GERMANY: G7 nations agree to watch forex markets, cooperate.
newsitem.headline: G7 nations agree to watch forex markets, cooperate.

text.p: Financial leaders of the world's top seven industrialised nations agreed on Saturday that major currencies have corrected their imbalances but vowed to monitor market movements and to cooperate, if necessary.

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said at the end of a Group of Seven (G7) meeting of finance ministers and central bank leaders that member's currencies should better reflect fundamentals and that excessive volatility was unfavourable.

Waigel, who said G7 nations had opted against issuing a communique, said leaders at the Berlin meeting had agreed "major misalignments in exchange markets," as noted in a G7 communique issued in April 1995, "have been corrected."

"We reaffirmed our views that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility is undesirable," Waigel, the meeting's chairman said in a statement issued at a news conference after the meeting ended.

Leaders at the meeting on Saturday had sent strong signals that they were comfortable with the dollar's appreciation from historic lows in the spring of 1995 but that the U.S. currency had now risen far enough.
But officials from Germany, Britain, Canada, France, Italy, Japan and the United States at the meeting equally warned it was now necessary for exchange rates to remain stable at current levels.

"We agreed to monitor developments on the currency markets and to coooperate as appropriate," Waigel said. G7 nations have sometimes resorted to currency market intervention to help steer currencies into appropriate ranges.
Member nations, however, stopped short of announcing a specific target for the dollar, as expected, but left no doubt that further gains would be against G7 desires.
